rounding.notes: Applied at publication only; all intermediate arithmetic is full-precision decimal. basket_cost carries more decimal places than dated_siu so the published print is reproducible from its own published figures. siu_per_usd truncates so it never overstates the work a dollar buys.

correction_notes.note: A reasoning-token cost gap affected this print: gemini-3.1-pro-preview's reasoning tokens (RunRecord.usage.reasoning — real, captured in every run record for this print) were not priced. packages/print/src/compute/class-cost.ts computed cost from usage.output alone. Reasoning tokens are billed by the provider at the output rate — confirmed live, 2026-09-08: Google's own published pricing states "Output price (including thinking tokens)", and a separate live check (xAI's real per-call billed cost) independently confirmed the same billing convention for reasoning models generally. This is not a methodology refinement — the index measures realised cost from executed runs, and the run records already carried this field. Corrected figures, computed from this print's own real run records and price snapshot with the fix applied, not from new data: this print's dated_siu was originally reported as $0.0120; the corrected figure is $0.0133. gemini-3.1-pro-preview's own basket cost was originally reported as $0.014049; the corrected figure is $0.020759. This print itself is not recomputed or replaced — the original stands, per the revision policy's unconditional never-edit guarantee. The fix (packages/print/src/compute/class-cost.ts, cost-of-production.ts) applies forward from the next published print onward, which will show a real, one-time jump in gemini-3.1-pro-preview's cost for this methodological reason, not a market move — see docs/methodology.md's Index governance.

This print includes gemini-3.1-pro-preview, whose Google Cloud billing predates the point where it was isolated to this project alone. Before that, a real, unexplained cost gap was found between Google's actual billed Gemini cost and this project's own computed cost on every day independently checked (2026-09-08 through 2026-09-10 -- 2026-09-08 far larger than the others, but the gap wasn't confined to that one day). This project's own per-token pricing was independently verified against Google's real published rates and confirmed correct, ruling out a calculation error on this project's side -- but the cause of the gap itself was never established, and Gemini's own real invoice cost for any day before isolation cannot be attributed to this project with confidence. Because that evidence gap cannot be reconstructed after the fact, this print will remain status: "provisional" permanently, not through neglect. See docs/methodology.md's Index governance (§7) for the general policy and the isolation fix that resolves this for prints going forward.

Correction to this print's own correction note above: that note framed the real-vs-computed Gemini cost gap around Google Cloud billing "isolation," implying a shared project or key might explain it. That's now confirmed wrong. The Gemini API key this project uses (siu-runs-prints, created 2026-08-30) has been dedicated solely to this project's SIU print runs since its creation -- no other Google Cloud project has ever used it. There was no shared-billing contamination to isolate, and moving it to its own dedicated project changed nothing that needed changing. The real gap -- a real ~2.7x cost spike on 2026-09-08 against every neighbouring day, and a persistent mismatch against the real, dated exchange rate found on every other day checked -- remains genuinely unexplained. This project's own per-token pricing was already independently verified against Google's real published rates and confirmed correct, so it isn't a calculation error on this project's side either. This print's status stays "provisional" for the honest reason that a real gap's real cause is still unknown -- not because a diagnosed shared-billing problem was found and fixed, which the correction note above incorrectly implied. See docs/methodology.md's Index governance (§7) for the current, corrected state of this investigation.
